Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors: 4-day history of sore throat (improving), nasal congestion with clear rhinorrhoea, new persistent dry cough, night sweats, intermittent headaches, myalgia, fatigue, mild exertional dyspnoea; afebrile since taking paracetamol/ibuprofen; occasional cigar smoking noted as a respiratory risk factor.  
- Relevant family medical history: Grandmother – type 2 diabetes; great-grandfather – eczema; no other conditions reported.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications): Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented); no regular prescription medicines.  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Usually attends gym but paused due to illness; reports drinking more fluids; mild reduction in appetite; further details not recorded.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Occasional cigar use at social/work events; occasional social alcohol; no illicit drug use reported.  
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded (denies ear pain or discharge).  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Reports “good stress” related to work; denies mood disturbance; no screening undertaken.  
- Vision problems or recent changes: Denies visual issues or photophobia.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Lives alone; employed as an accountant; no caring responsibilities mentioned.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Acute self-limited upper respiratory symptoms (sore throat → rhinitis → dry cough) with mild systemic features (myalgia, night sweats, fatigue) and no red-flag signs. No significant comorbidities.

Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx):
• Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold) – High likelihood given typical progression and improving course.  
• Influenza – Moderate likelihood; systemic symptoms fit but fever short-lived.  
• COVID-19 (mild) – Moderate likelihood due to overlapping URI symptoms, night sweats, exertional dyspnoea, and workplace exposure.

Working diagnosis: Probable viral URTI (common cold vs early flu/COVID-19).  

Management priorities: Symptomatic care, monitoring for deterioration, ensure rest and hydration, safety-net advice, follow-up if no improvement or red-flag symptoms develop.

Management Plan

- Advised rest and consider 1–2 days off work.  
- Increase oral fluids; maintain light diet as tolerated.  
- Continue Paracetamol and/or Ibuprofen as needed for fever, pain (doses per package directions).  
- Red-flag advice: Return or call sooner for high fever, worsening breathlessness, chest pain, persistent or worsening symptoms beyond one week.  
- Routine review/telehealth follow-up in 1 week if not improving.  
- Offered ongoing support for stress or mood concerns if needed.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded (patient currently coping).  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection – High: Classic symptom sequence, mild course, improving with conservative care.  
2. Influenza – Moderate: Abrupt onset systemic symptoms; watch for persistence/severity.  
3. COVID-19 (mild) – Moderate: Symptom overlap incl. night sweats and exertional dyspnoea; consider testing per local guidelines.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs, physical examination findings, BMI, immunisation review (incl. flu/COVID boosters), alcohol and smoking quantity assessment, mental health screening, urinalysis, preventive health status (e.g., cardiovascular risk, blood tests).  
● No internal contradictions between transcript and DDx identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear history; no physical examination possible due to telehealth; no major inaudible sections.
